word:hebrew:H1064.explanation: Bekorath is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H108.explanation: Ed means a fog or mist.

word:hebrew:H1158.explanation: Ba'a means to swell. It can also mean to inquire or ask.

word:hebrew:H1239.explanation: Baqar means to seek out or search. It can describe examining something closely. It can also mean making an inquiry.

word:hebrew:H1266.explanation: Beroth refers to a tree. In this passage, it is rendered as fir.

word:hebrew:H131.explanation: This word refers to “Adummim,” a named place in the Old Testament. It functions as a place-name rather than as a general description or action. It appears twice, both times in Joshua, in passages that identify locations within Israel’s boundaries. Since no broader definition is provided, its ordinary meaning is best understood as the name Adummim itself. The surrounding wording determines the place’s specific role in each boundary description.

word:hebrew:H1363.explanation: Gôbahh means pride or arrogance. It can also refer to physical height.

word:hebrew:H1477.explanation: The word refers to “Gunites,” a named group or family designation. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Numbers 26:48, and its English rendering consistently identifies this group as Gunites. The word itself names the people rather than describing an action, quality, or abstract idea. Because the surrounding verse text is not included here, the entry establishes the group’s name but does not explain their specific role in that passage.

word:hebrew:H1532.explanation: This Hebrew word is a noun referring to a “barber,” someone whose work involves cutting or shaving hair. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Ezekiel 5:1. The word identifies the person or professional tool-user being referred to, while the surrounding verse determines its specific role in that passage. Its basic meaning remains focused on a barber rather than on a broader description of grooming or hair itself.

word:hebrew:H1590.explanation: Gannab means a thief or stealer.

word:hebrew:H1819.explanation: Damâh means to compare or liken one thing to another. It can also describe what someone thinks or devises.

word:hebrew:H1846.explanation: Daak means to be extinguished or put out.

word:hebrew:H1903.explanation: Hagin may mean suitable or turning; here it is rendered directly.

word:hebrew:H197.explanation: Ulam means a vestibule or porch attached to a building.

word:hebrew:H1994.explanation: Himmow means “they,” referring to more than one person. It can also mean “those,” referring to multiple things.

word:hebrew:H203.explanation: On refers to a person named On. It functions as a personal name rather than as a common description or action. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Numbers 16:1, and the English rendering is “On.” Because the available passage evidence does not include the verse text or surrounding context, the name’s particular role in that passage cannot be explained further here. Its basic meaning in the biblical record is therefore the identification of this individual.

word:hebrew:H2043.explanation: Hararite is a designation for a person. Shammah and Ahiam are each called Hararite.

word:hebrew:H2142.explanation: Zakar means to remember or bring to remembrance.

word:hebrew:H2205.explanation: Zaqen means old or aged. It can also refer to elders as a group; officers are described as being over them.

word:hebrew:H2270.explanation: Châbêr means an associate, companion, or fellow. It can also describe people knit together as one.

word:hebrew:H2357.explanation: This Hebrew word means “pale.” It describes a change or condition in which someone or something loses its normal color, functioning as an action word rather than naming a person, place, or object. The word appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Isaiah 29:22, so its precise force there depends on the surrounding verse and passage. Its central lexical idea is a loss of normal color.

word:hebrew:H2436.explanation: Cheiq means bosom, literally a place where something is held close. Figuratively, it can describe a close relationship, as in “the wife of your bosom.”

word:hebrew:H2469.explanation: Heldai is a personal name used for two different men in the Hebrew Old Testament. It is not presented here as an ordinary descriptive word, action, or quality, but as a name identifying a person. The name appears twice in the Hebrew corpus: once in 1 Chronicles 27:15 and once in Zechariah 6:10. Since both occurrences render it as “Heldai,” its precise significance as a name is not explained by these records alone.

word:hebrew:H2520.explanation: Helkath is a Hebrew place-name. It identifies a location rather than expressing an action, quality, or ordinary object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs twice, both times in Joshua: once in Joshua 19:25 and again in Joshua 21:31. The available renderings preserve the name as “Helkath,” so no additional English meaning is established here. Its precise significance in either passage depends on the surrounding verse and the location’s role in that passage.

word:hebrew:H2555.explanation: Chamas means violence. It can also describe injustice.

word:hebrew:H2582.explanation: Chenadad is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H2601.explanation: Hanameel is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H27.explanation: Abidan is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Abidan,” rather than an ordinary descriptive word. It functions as a name identifying a person in the Hebrew Old Testament. The name occurs five times, all in Numbers, from Numbers 1:11 through Numbers 10:24. No broader lexical definition is available here, so its supported meaning is the name itself; the surrounding verse supplies any further identification or significance.

word:hebrew:H2744.explanation: Harhur is a Hebrew name preserved as Harhur in English Bible translations. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, once in Ezra 2:51 and once in Nehemiah 7:53. Since the available wording gives no descriptive definition, the name itself is the clearest supported meaning. It identifies a person or family listed among those connected with the returned community, though the precise identity cannot be explained from the name alone. Its two occurrences are in parallel lists of names.

word:hebrew:H2818.explanation: Chashach means to need something. It can also describe something that is necessary.

word:hebrew:H2821.explanation: Chashak means to be dark or to darken something. The land is darkened, and the stars are dark.

word:hebrew:H2887.explanation: Tebeth is a Hebrew proper name, rendered “Tebeth,” rather than a descriptive word. It appears once in the Hebrew corpus, at Esther 2:16, so its function there is to identify something by name rather than to describe an action or quality. The available wording does not provide a broader definition or enough surrounding verse text to explain more specifically here.

word:hebrew:H2933.explanation: Tamah means to be impure in a religious sense or defiled; it can also describe being regarded as vile.

word:hebrew:H294.explanation: Ahisamach is a Hebrew personal name, identifying an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or object. It appears three times in the Old Testament, all in Exodus: 31:6, 35:34, and 38:23. The name is associated with passages involving giving and commands, but the available wording does not provide a separate lexical definition or explain the name’s underlying meaning. Thus, its ordinary role is to identify the person called Ahisamach.

word:hebrew:H3174.explanation: Jehiah is a Hebrew personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing a general action, quality, or object. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, at 1 Chronicles 15:24, and English Bible renderings preserve it as “Jehiah.” Because the available information identifies this word as a name but does not provide a broader lexical definition, its main significance is naming the person designated in that passage. The surrounding verse gives the context for understanding Jehiah’s role there.

word:hebrew:H319.explanation: Acharith means the end or the last part. It can also refer to future time, including the latter days.

word:hebrew:H3237.explanation: This Hebrew word is a rare term whose precise meaning cannot be stated confidently from the available lexical information. It occurs only once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Judges 16:26. The word’s identity is preserved, but no short definition, English rendering, or approved fallback meaning is available. Its exact sense therefore must be determined from the verse and its surrounding context rather than from this word-level entry alone.

word:hebrew:H3291.explanation: Jaakobah is a Hebrew personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing a general action, quality, or object. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 1 Chronicles 4:36, and the English rendering preserves it as “Jaakobah.” Because the surrounding verse text is not included here, the name’s particular role in that genealogy must be understood from its context; its basic lexical function is simply to identify the person named Jaakobah.

word:hebrew:H3325.explanation: Yitshari means a Jitsharite, a descendant of Jitshar.

word:hebrew:H3350.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “burning.” It names the idea or condition of burning, giving a concise description rather than identifying a person, place, or specific object. It occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, and both occurrences are found in Isaiah 10:16. Because the available wording is consistent, “burning” is the clearest supported sense. Its exact force in that verse must be understood from the surrounding passage, but the word’s basic meaning remains focused on burning.

word:hebrew:H3413.explanation: Jeremai is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H3484.explanation: Jeshurun is a symbolic name for Israel.

word:hebrew:H3651.explanation: Ken means so or thus, expressing that something is in the stated way. It can also mean rightly or right, describing what is correct. In another context, it marks sequence, meaning after that.

word:hebrew:H3668.explanation: Kenaanah is a personal name used for two Israelites.

word:hebrew:H3729.explanation: Kephath means to fetter or bind, as when men are bound before being cast into a fiery furnace.

word:hebrew:H3776.explanation: This Hebrew word means “lamb,” naming the animal identified by the text. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Leviticus 5:6, so its normal lexical sense is supported by that occurrence and its consistent English rendering. Readers can understand it as the name of the animal itself, while the verse supplies the specific action or requirement associated with it. Its particular role in that verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H3817.explanation: Leummim is a Hebrew name rendered “Leummim.” It functions as a name rather than as an ordinary descriptive word. The term appears only once in the Hebrew Bible, at Genesis 25:3, and its setting is connected with genealogy and birth or begetting. Because no explicit definition or surrounding verse text is available here, the safest understanding is the name itself, not an expanded meaning or interpretation. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H3930.explanation: Loa means the gullet, or throat.

word:hebrew:H3945.explanation: Latsats means to deride or scorn.

word:hebrew:H3992.explanation: Ma’ar means to be bitter or to embitter, with a painful effect.

word:hebrew:H4067.explanation: Madon means stature, or height. It refers to a man’s great stature.

word:hebrew:H4113.explanation: Mahămôrâh may refer to an abyss. It can also mean a deep pit.

word:hebrew:H4184.explanation: Mûwsh means to touch or feel, and it can also describe handling something.

word:hebrew:H4229.explanation: Mâchâh means to erase or wipe away. It can also mean to destroy.

word:hebrew:H4276.explanation: Machatsith means a halving or half of something.

word:hebrew:H4351.explanation: Mekurah refers to origin or birth. It can also refer to a habitation.

word:hebrew:H4368.explanation: Mekonah is a proper name rather than an ordinary descriptive word. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Nehemiah 11:28, and is rendered “Mekonah.” The available information identifies how the word is presented, but does not provide a separate definition or enough surrounding verse text to establish whether it names a person, place, or another specific entity. Its precise referent therefore depends on the passage’s full context.

word:hebrew:H4474.explanation: Mimshal means rule or dominion. It can describe a king’s dominion and sons ruling over their father’s house.

word:hebrew:H449.explanation: Elidad is a Hebrew personal name, referring to a specific man rather than expressing a general idea or action. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Numbers 34:21, and is rendered as “Elidad.” The name itself does not provide a stated definition of its components, so its ordinary function is identification: it distinguishes this individual from others in the passage. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H4625.explanation: Maʻăqâsh means a crook in a road or a crooked thing.

word:hebrew:H4650.explanation: Mêphîyts means a breaker, that is, a mallet or maul.

word:hebrew:H4737.explanation: Miqneyahu is an Israelite personal name, rendered Mikneiah in English.

word:hebrew:H4791.explanation: Marom means height or an elevated place. It can also describe what is above.

word:hebrew:H4852.explanation: Mesha is a Hebrew name rendered as “Mesha” in English. It functions as a specific designation rather than a general description or action word, so its meaning is identifying rather than describing a quality. This word appears once in the Hebrew Bible corpus, at Genesis 10:30. Without the verse text, it is not possible to establish from this record whether Mesha refers to a person, place, or region.

word:hebrew:H4948.explanation: Mishqal means weight. It can also refer to weighing.

word:hebrew:H4971.explanation: Mathkôneth means proportion. It can describe the composition of something or refer to a measure.

word:hebrew:H5024.explanation: Nâbach means to bark, as a dog.

word:hebrew:H5110.explanation: Nûwd means to nod or waver, as a reed is shaken.

word:hebrew:H5226.explanation: Nekach means before, opposite, or against. It marks one thing’s position in relation to another, as when one place is opposite another.

word:hebrew:H5279.explanation: Naamah is a personal name. It names a woman, an Ammonitess, and a place.

word:hebrew:H5323.explanation: Natsa means to go away or flee.

word:hebrew:H535.explanation: Amal means to droop or languish, describing weakness or feebleness in people, land, and plants. It can also describe mourning.

word:hebrew:H540.explanation: Aman means to believe, to be faithful, or to be sure.

policy.priorReviewerNotes: The lexical evidence supports “to hem in” or “bind,” but Song 7:3 describes breasts like twin fawns and does not directly support that sense. Therefore the required Scripture evidence is invalid for the claim.

word:hebrew:H5622.explanation: Çarbal means a cloak or coat.

word:hebrew:H5680.explanation: Ibrîy means Hebrew, an Eberite or descendant of Eber. Scripture applies this designation to Abram and to Hebrew women.

word:hebrew:H5789.explanation: This Hebrew word is a verb whose precise meaning cannot be established from the available lexical information. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Joel 4:11, and no approved English meaning or short definition is available for it. The verse reference identifies its location, but without the verse text and a recognized meaning, it would be unsafe to assign a sense or describe the action it expresses. Its role must therefore be understood from the surrounding passage and further lexical evidence.

word:hebrew:H5815.explanation: Aziel is a personal name, referring to one individual rather than describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in 1 Chronicles 15:20, and English renderings preserve it as “Aziel.” Because personal names identify people, the name’s lexical entry does not by itself explain the person’s character, role, or significance in that passage. Those details belong to the surrounding verse and account, not to the name alone.

word:hebrew:H5860.explanation: ʻÎyṭ means to swoop down upon, literally or figuratively.

word:hebrew:H6003.explanation: Amalekite means an individual Amalekite, while Amalekites can refer to the people collectively.

word:hebrew:H6119.explanation: Aqeb means heel, the back part of the foot. It can also refer to a horse's hoof. Figuratively, it can refer to what is last.

word:hebrew:H6212.explanation: Êseb means grass or a tender shoot, including herbs.

word:hebrew:H6308.explanation: Pâda means to retrieve or deliver.

word:hebrew:H6331.explanation: Pur means to bring something to nothing.

word:hebrew:H6397.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to someone identified as “Pelonite,” functioning as a personal designation rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. It appears three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, all in 1 Chronicles. English translations consistently render it “Pelonite,” so the word’s basic sense is limited to identifying a person by this designation. The surrounding verse text would be needed to explain that individual’s particular role or significance in each passage.

word:hebrew:H6407.explanation: Paltite is a Hebrew personal designation rendered “Paltite.” It functions as a proper identifying name rather than a general quality, action, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in 2 Samuel 23:26, and the English renderings consistently preserve it as “Paltite.” The available information identifies the designation but does not provide a broader ordinary meaning or enough surrounding verse text to explain anything beyond its use as a name. Its precise significance in that verse belongs to the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H6498.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to gourds, a kind of plant or fruit. It appears only once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in 2 Kings 4:39, and functions as the name of something gathered from the field and used as food. The word itself identifies the plant or its fruit; the surrounding verse is needed to explain the danger or outcome associated with it. Its ordinary meaning is therefore concrete and agricultural: gourds rather than an abstract idea or action.

word:hebrew:H6586.explanation: Pâshaʻ means to break away from just authority. It can describe transgressing against someone or revolting from under another’s rule.

word:hebrew:H6616.explanation: Pathil means twine. It can also refer to a lace used to bind or fasten.

word:hebrew:H6649.explanation: “Zibeon” is a personal name, used to identify an individual in the Hebrew Old Testament. It does not function as a common description or action word, so its significance here is the person it names rather than a separate abstract meaning. The name appears eight times across seven Old Testament verses, chiefly in Genesis 36 and also in 1 Chronicles 1. These passages place Zibeon within genealogical records and family relationships.

word:hebrew:H6735.explanation: Tsiyr means a hinge; it can also refer to pain or pangs, or to a messenger or ambassador. It names the hinges on which a door turns. It can describe the pains of childbirth. A messenger or ambassador is someone sent by another.

word:hebrew:H6858.explanation: Tsepheth means the capital, or chapiter, at the top of a column.

word:hebrew:H6861.explanation: Tsiqlon means a sack tied at the mouth and can also refer to a husk.

word:hebrew:H6964.explanation: Kolaiah is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than describing an action, quality, or object. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, rendered consistently as “Kolaiah.” The name identifies people mentioned in Nehemiah 11:7 and Jeremiah 29:21. Its precise significance as a name is not stated in the supplied passages, so its ordinary biblical function is identification: it distinguishes a particular person within the surrounding account.

word:hebrew:H698.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “spoils,” the things taken as a result of conquest or victory. It functions as something acted upon, rather than naming the person or action involved. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Isaiah 25:11. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding verse text, but its basic meaning points to spoils as an object associated with taking or possessing.

word:hebrew:H7048.explanation: Qallâçâh means ridicule or mocking. It can describe someone made an object of mocking before all countries.

word:hebrew:H7071.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “Kanah,” a named place in the Old Testament. It functions as a proper place-name rather than a general descriptive term. The word occurs three times in the Hebrew Old Testament, and all three occurrences are in Joshua, in descriptions of territorial boundaries. Its references are Joshua 16:8, Joshua 17:9, and Joshua 19:28. The surrounding verse text would provide the local details, but the word itself identifies the place called Kanah.

word:hebrew:H7152.explanation: Qeriyoth is the name of two places, rendered Kerioth in English.

word:hebrew:H7185.explanation: Qashah means hard, tough, or severe. Depending on the context, it can describe hard labor, cruelty, or a hardened refusal to listen.

word:hebrew:H7206.explanation: This word means “Reubenites,” referring to the people belonging to the tribe or family of Reuben. It functions as a designation for that Israelite group, appearing in passages that describe their inheritance, tribal territory, speech, and responsibilities. The word occurs 18 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, including references in Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, and 1 Chronicles. Its normal sense identifies the descendants or members of Reuben rather than describing an action or quality.

word:hebrew:H7259.explanation: Ribkah is the name rendered Rebekah, and Rebekah was Isaac’s wife.

word:hebrew:H7417.explanation: Rimmon is a proper name. It names places, including a rock called Rimmon.

word:hebrew:H7488.explanation: Raʻănân means verdant or green. It can also describe something flourishing.

word:hebrew:H7530.explanation: Retseph is a place in Assyria, rendered Rezeph in English.

word:hebrew:H7545.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to a confection, especially a prepared mixture made from fragrant ingredients. It is used only twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in Exodus 30, in instructions concerning the holy anointing oil and incense. The word functions as the object of making or preparing, pointing to the finished compound rather than to a single ingredient. Its precise significance in either verse depends on the surrounding instructions, but its basic sense is a carefully blended, aromatic preparation.

word:hebrew:H7592.explanation: Sha'al means to inquire or ask. It can also mean to request something. It may extend to demanding or requiring something.

word:hebrew:H7602.explanation: Shaaph means to inhale eagerly, as in panting. It can also describe earnestly desiring something or swallowing someone up. In another use, it means hastening.

word:hebrew:H7813.explanation: Sâchû means a pond for swimming.

word:hebrew:H786.explanation: ʼIsh means “there is” or “there are,” expressing that something exists.

word:hebrew:H7884.explanation: Shihor-libnath is a Hebrew geographical name, referring to a particular location rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, it occurs twice, with both occurrences in Joshua 19:26. Its function is to identify a specific place within the biblical account. The available information does not establish the location’s precise meaning, boundaries, or significance beyond its use as a named geographic place.

policy.priorReviewerNotes: The Scripture evidence supports “peace,” but LEX_DEF gives “prosperity,” and the candidate presents the gloss/rendering as the sole primary meaning while mapping LEX_DEF as support. Thus the primary claim does not accurately match all required lexical evidence.

word:hebrew:H8038.explanation: Shemeber is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Shemeber,” rather than a common word describing an action, quality, or object. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Genesis 14:2, and functions as the name of an individual in the biblical record. Because it is a name and appears only once, Scripture provides no broader recurring usage from which to develop an expanded lexical meaning. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H8144.explanation: Shani means the color crimson or scarlet. It can also describe material of that color, including a scarlet thread.

word:hebrew:H8236.explanation: This Hebrew word is a personal name rendered “Shiphrah.” It functions as a name rather than as a general description, action, or quality. The name occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Exodus 1:15. The available scriptural connections place Shiphrah in spoken interaction and in a birth-related setting, but the word itself supplies the person’s name, not a further definition. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H8269.explanation: Sar means a chief or ruler, a person who holds authority. Depending on the passage, it can refer to princes, captains, or a governor.

word:hebrew:H8320.explanation: Saruk means bright red, a bay color. It can also describe something speckled, as in a horse’s coloring.

word:hebrew:H8382.explanation: Ta'am describes things joined together or made double. It can also describe a sheep in a flock bearing twins.

word:hebrew:H8405.explanation: Têbêts is the name of a place in Palestine, rendered as Thebez.

word:hebrew:H8470.explanation: The word refers to “Tahanites,” functioning as a group name rather than a description of an action or quality. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, at Numbers 26:35, and the available English renderings agree on this designation. Its exact role in that verse depends on the surrounding context, but its basic function is to identify the people named by it.

word:hebrew:H8557.explanation: Temes describes melting away or disappearing.

word:hebrew:H863.explanation: Ittai is a personal name. It is also rendered Ithai.

word:hebrew:H8643.explanation: Teru'ah means a loud shout. It can describe joyful shouting in praise or an alarm. It can also refer to trumpet blasts used to sound an alarm.

word:hebrew:H939.explanation: Buwzah means something scorned or an object of contempt—something despised.

word:hebrew:H966.explanation: Bezek is a Hebrew proper name, used to identify “Bezek” rather than to describe an action, quality, or object. It functions as a name in the Old Testament and does not have an explicit descriptive definition in the available material. The word occurs three times in the Hebrew Old Testament: twice in Judges and once in 1 Samuel. Its precise significance in any one passage depends on the surrounding verse and context.
